lastText: File ClosedStimson's Warning, IgnoredThe Joint Chiefs of Staff, 1940–1945Kyoto, not Hiroshima, took the first weapon. Over a thousand years of temples, shrines, and archives with no second copy anywhere in the world went with the people who were there to tend them, at a scale the historical Hiroshima toll didn't reach, in a city the firebombing campaign had deliberately left untouched specifically so the weapon's effects could be measured against an intact baseline. Stimson's own real, documented fear, that a loss like this would poison whatever relationship the occupation needed to build afterward, was treated here as one wartime cost among many rather than a condition requiring its own answer. Whether that reads, to the country being occupied, as consistency or as indifference was never actually decided.
